questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Which part do we see with?
questions.explanation: We see with our eyes. Ears are for hearing and the nose is for smelling.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: We smell with our ___.
questions.explanation: We smell with our nose. Breathe in and sniff a flower!

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Match each part to what it finds out.
questions.explanation: Eyes see colours, ears hear sounds, a nose smells flowers and a tongue tastes a sour lemon.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Which part do we taste with?
questions.explanation: We taste with our tongue. It tells us if food is sweet or sour.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Scientists ask questions.
questions.explanation: Yes! Scientists ask "What is it?" and "What will happen if…?" Asking questions helps us learn.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Rafi wants to see a tiny ant. Which tool helps?
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass makes small things look bigger, so we can look closely.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Tap all the tools a scientist uses.
questions.explanation: Scientists look closely with a magnifying glass, measure with a ruler and check how hot things are with a thermometer. A lollipop and a teddy are not tools.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Feel and sort. Is it soft or hard?
questions.explanation: A sponge, a teddy and wool are soft and squishy. A brick, a rock and a spoon are hard.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Put the science steps in order.
questions.explanation: A scientist asks a question, makes a guess, tries it out, and then looks to see what happened.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Which one will float in water?
questions.explanation: Wood floats on water. A key and a coin are heavy for their size, so they sink.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Tap all the things that float.
questions.explanation: A leaf, a ball and wood float on water. A rock, a key and a coin sink. Try it in a bowl of water to check!

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Rafi guessed a key would float. It sank. His guess was wrong.
questions.explanation: Yes. Scientists check their guess by trying it. Rafi saw the key sink, so his guess was wrong, and that is fine because we learn something.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Nadia finds a berry in the garden. What should she do?
questions.explanation: Only taste food that a grown-up gives you. Some berries are not safe to eat, so always ask a grown-up first.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Anika feels something in a bag. Which part helps her?
questions.explanation: We touch and feel with our hands. Our skin tells us if something is soft, hard, hot or cold.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: We heard 4 birds, 6 cars, 2 bells. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 6 is more than 4 and more than 2. We heard the most cars.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Put them in order, smallest to biggest.
questions.explanation: We compare things to see which is bigger. An ant is the smallest, then a mouse, a cat and an elephant is the biggest.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Match each tool to its job.
questions.explanation: A magnifying glass helps us look closely, a ruler measures, a camera takes a picture and a pencil draws what we see.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: We can draw a picture to show what we found.
questions.explanation: Yes. Scientists draw, take pictures and colour graphs so they can remember and tell others what they found.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Eyes shut, you shake a box. Which two parts help?
questions.explanation: Your hands feel the box shake and your ears hear the rattle. Your eyes are shut, so they cannot help.

questions.title: Little Explorers
questions.stem: Raju says the stone floats. Mina says it sinks. What next?
questions.explanation: We find out by trying it! Put the stone in water and look. Voting or guessing again cannot tell us what really happens.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A dog is a living thing.
questions.explanation: Yes. A dog grows, eats, moves and has puppies, so it is living.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Living or non-living?
questions.explanation: Cats, fish, flowers and ants grow, need food or water, and make young. A teddy, a car, a chair and a rock were never alive.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Which one is a living thing?
questions.explanation: A tree grows, drinks water and makes seeds, so it is living. A rock and a chair do not grow.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Which one is a non-living thing?
questions.explanation: A car was never alive. It does not grow, eat or have babies. A fish and a flower are living.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A plant needs water and ___ to grow.
questions.explanation: Plants drink water and need sunlight to grow. Toys and sweets are not food for plants.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A rock can grow like a plant.
questions.explanation: No. A rock is non-living. It does not grow, eat or have babies. A plant grows from a tiny seed.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Tap all the things living things need.
questions.explanation: Living things need food, water, air, a home and care. A TV and a toy are fun, but we do not need them to live.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Match each baby to its grown-up.
questions.explanation: Living things grow up. A chick grows into a hen, a little plant grows into a tree and a baby grows into a grown-up.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Put Mina's seed story in order.
sequence: She gives it water and sun.
questions.explanation: A seed in soil needs water and sunshine. It sends up a green shoot and slowly grows into a tall plant.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Mina's plant looks droopy and dry. What does it need?
questions.explanation: A dry, droopy plant needs water. Sweets and toys cannot help a plant.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Nadia has a kitten. Tap what the kitten needs.
questions.explanation: A kitten needs food, water and a safe, warm home, like all animals. A TV or a car is of no use to it.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Joy sees a strange bug. What should he do?
questions.explanation: Look with your eyes and do not touch bugs you do not know. Some can bite or sting. Wash your hands after exploring.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: What do we need to see cells?
questions.explanation: Cells are the tiny building blocks of living things. They are so small that we need a microscope to see them.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Living things are made of tiny ___.
questions.explanation: All living things are made of tiny parts called cells. Cells are so small we need a microscope to see them.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Which one can grow, eat and have babies?
questions.explanation: A cow grows, eats grass and has calves. A ball and a chair are non-living.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: We found 5 ants, 3 birds, 2 flowers. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 5 is more than 3 and more than 2. We found the most ants.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A plant grows from a tiny seed.
questions.explanation: Yes. Plants are living things. A seed grows into a little plant and then a big plant.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A toy car moves. A snail moves. Which one is living?
questions.explanation: Moving is not enough. A snail eats, grows and has babies. A toy car only moves when someone pushes it or it has a motor.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: Put the chick pictures in order.
questions.explanation: A chick grows inside an egg. It hatches, is a fluffy chick, and then grows into a hen.

questions.title: Living and Non-living Things
questions.stem: A teddy bear is a living thing.
questions.explanation: No. A teddy bear does not eat, grow or have babies. It was never alive.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Match each animal to how it moves.
questions.explanation: Rabbits hop, birds fly, fish swim and snails slide along slowly. Animals move in different ways.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Tap all the animals that can fly.
questions.explanation: Birds have wings and feathers. Butterflies and bees are insects with wings, so they fly too. Fish swim and cows walk.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Which one is an animal?
questions.explanation: A duck is an animal. It moves, eats and has ducklings. A tree and a flower are plants.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Tap all the animals that live in water.
questions.explanation: Fish, crabs and dolphins live in water. Cats, cows and dogs live on land.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: An elephant uses its trunk to pick up food.
questions.explanation: Yes. An elephant uses its long trunk like a hand to pick up food and to drink water.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Sort the animals by how they move.
questions.explanation: Fish and dolphins swim. Birds and butterflies fly. Cats and cows walk or run on land.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Match each animal to what it gives us.
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk, hens give us eggs, bees make honey and sheep give us wool. Animals help us in many ways.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A cow gives us ___ to drink.
questions.explanation: Cows give us milk. Hens give us eggs, bees make honey and sheep give us wool.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Put Nana's hen story in order.
sequence: The hen sits on her eggs.
Chicks come out of the eggs.
questions.explanation: A hen keeps her eggs warm. Chicks hatch, eat and grow bigger every day until they are hens too.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A baby animal grows into a grown-up animal.
questions.explanation: Yes. Animal babies eat and grow bigger, just like you. A chick grows into a hen and a calf grows into a cow.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A cow lays eggs.
questions.explanation: No. Hens lay eggs. A cow gives us milk.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Bees make honey.
questions.explanation: Yes. Honeybees make honey from flower nectar. Animals help us in many ways.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Look at the snail. How does it move?
questions.image_alt: A snail with a spiral shell.
questions.explanation: A snail slides along slowly on one soft foot. It cannot hop or fly.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A bird lays its eggs in a ___.
questions.explanation: Birds build nests, often in trees. The mother bird keeps the eggs warm until the chicks hatch.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Tuli wears a woollen shawl. Which animal gave the wool?
questions.explanation: Sheep grow thick wool. People cut it, spin it into yarn and make warm clothes. Hens and fish do not have wool.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Sumi wants to see a fish. Where should she look?
questions.explanation: Fish live in water, in ponds, rivers and the sea. They breathe in the water and cannot live in trees or the sky.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: Rafi sees a strange dog near the road. What should he do?
questions.explanation: Do not touch animals you do not know. Even a friendly looking dog may bite. Tell a grown-up.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: This is a chick. What will it grow into?
questions.explanation: A chick grows into a hen. Baby animals grow into grown-ups of the same kind.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: I hop. I have long ears. Who am I?
questions.explanation: A rabbit hops on strong back legs and has long ears. A cat walks and a fish swims.

questions.title: Animals Around Us
questions.stem: A hen sits on 3 eggs. All hatch. How many chicks?
questions.explanation: Each egg hatches one chick. 3 eggs make 3 chicks.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Look at the plant. Which number is the flower?
questions.image_alt: A plant with a flower at the top, leaves, a stem, a fruit and roots under the ground, each marked with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 1 is the flower, at the top of the plant. Number 2 is a leaf and number 3 is the stem.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Which number shows the roots under the ground?
questions.image_alt: A plant with a flower at the top, leaves, a stem, a fruit and roots under the ground, each marked with a number.
questions.explanation: Number 4 is the roots. Roots grow under the ground.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Number 5 is the fruit.
questions.image_alt: A plant with a flower at the top, leaves, a stem, a fruit and roots under the ground, each marked with a number.
questions.explanation: Yes. Number 5 is the fruit. Fruits grow on plants and hold the seeds.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Match each word to its picture.
questions.explanation: Fruit, vegetables and rice all come from plants. Plants help us with our food.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Tap what a plant needs to grow.
questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight and water to grow. Sweets, ice cream and balls cannot help a plant grow.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Roots grow under the ___.
questions.explanation: Roots grow under the ground, in the soil. The leaves and flowers are above the ground.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Put the seed story in order.
sequence: A seed is in the soil.
questions.explanation: A seed in the soil gets water and warmth. A shoot comes up, leaves grow, and later the plant makes flowers.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Sort the plants.
questions.explanation: Palm and other trees are tall plants with a trunk. Roses and sunflowers are flowers. Carrots and broccoli are vegetables we eat.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Plants need water to grow.
questions.explanation: Yes. Plants drink water. They also need sunlight to grow well.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A bean plant grows best in a dark cupboard.
questions.explanation: No. Without light a bean plant grows pale, thin and weak. It grows best by a window where there is light.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A plant has roots under the ground.
questions.explanation: Yes. Roots grow under the ground. Leaves, flowers and fruit grow above it.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Moung's bean plant is under the bed. Where should it go?
questions.explanation: Plants need light. A window lets sunlight in, so the bean plant can grow green and strong.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Rafi is hot. Where can he sit in the shade?
questions.explanation: A big tree gives cool shade. Trees help us in many ways.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Grandpa's mango tree is big. Tap what it gives.
questions.explanation: A mango tree gives sweet fruit, cool shade and a safe home for birds. It does not give a car or a TV.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Which one is a fruit?
questions.explanation: An apple is a fruit. It grows on a tree and has seeds inside. Broccoli and potatoes are vegetables.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Which one is a baby plant?
questions.explanation: A seedling is a baby plant that has just grown from a seed. It will grow bigger.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A seed grows into a ___.
questions.explanation: A tiny seed, with water and sunlight, grows into a plant.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Two beans: one in light, one in dark. Which grows strong?
questions.explanation: The bean in the light grows green and strong. The bean in the dark grows pale, thin and weak, because plants need light.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: A: sun. B: water. C: sun, water. Which grows best?
questions.explanation: Plants need both sunlight and water. C gets both, so it grows best.

questions.title: Plants Around Us
questions.stem: Tap all the things plants give us.
questions.explanation: Mangoes, wood and carrots come from plants. Milk comes from cows and cars are made in factories.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Look at the body. Which number is the head?
questions.image_alt: A child with body parts marked by numbers: head, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, hand, chest, tummy, leg, knee and foot.
questions.explanation: Number 1 is the head. Our eyes, ears, nose and mouth are on our head.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Which number is the hand?
questions.image_alt: A child with body parts marked by numbers: head, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, hand, chest, tummy, leg, knee and foot.
questions.explanation: Number 6 is the hand. We use our hands to hold, touch and wave.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Which number is the knee?
questions.image_alt: A child with body parts marked by numbers: head, neck, shoulder, arm, elbow, hand, chest, tummy, leg, knee and foot.
questions.explanation: Number 10 is the knee. It bends in the middle of the leg. Number 5 is the elbow in the arm.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Match each part to its sense.
questions.explanation: Eyes see, ears hear, the nose smells, the tongue tastes and our skin and hands touch. These are our five senses.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Match each part to what it finds.
questions.explanation: Ears hear music, a nose smells a flower, a tongue tastes sweet honey and our hands feel cold ice.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Tap the parts we use to walk and run.
questions.explanation: We use our legs and our feet to walk and run. Ears are for hearing and eyes are for seeing.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Tuli wears glasses. Which sense do they help?
questions.explanation: Glasses help Tuli see clearly. Her eyes help her to read, play and learn.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: We hear with our ___.
questions.explanation: We hear with our ears. They help us enjoy music and know when someone calls us.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: We have five senses.
questions.explanation: Yes. We see, hear, smell, taste and touch. The five senses help us find out about the world.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Children are all exactly the same.
questions.explanation: No. We are the same in some ways, like having eyes and hands. We are different in our hair, height and clothes. That is what makes each of us special.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Put them in order, youngest to oldest.
questions.explanation: We start as a baby, grow into a child, then a grown-up, and later we become older.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Sort the body parts: head, arms or legs?
questions.explanation: Eyes, ears and nose are on our head. Hands and arms are together. Legs and feet help us walk.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Mina smells smoke in the kitchen. Which part tells her?
questions.explanation: Our nose smells smoke and warns us of danger. Mina should tell a grown-up straight away.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: How can Tuli look after her eyes?
questions.explanation: Tuli should wear her glasses and not sit too close to the TV. We should also never look at the Sun.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Mina smells and tastes a cake. Which two parts does she use?
questions.explanation: She smells the cake with her nose and tastes it with her tongue. Her foot cannot help and her ear is for hearing.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: You are bigger now than when you were a baby.
questions.explanation: Yes. Since you were born you have grown taller and stronger. Growing is a sign of being alive.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: Tap what children have.
questions.explanation: Children have eyes, ears and hands. We are the same in many ways. What we wear or play with can be different.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: We feel hot and cold with our ___.
questions.explanation: Our skin helps us touch and feel things. It tells us if something is hot, cold, soft or rough.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: You hold your nose and taste a mango. What happens?
questions.explanation: Smell and taste work together. When you hold your nose, it is harder to taste.

questions.title: My Body and My Senses
questions.stem: A cat has big ears. What can it do well?
questions.explanation: Animals use their senses too. A cat can hear small sounds, like a mouse moving.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Sort the foods. Every day or only a treat?
questions.explanation: Tomatoes, fish and rice are good to eat every day. Burgers, cake and lollipops are treats: just a little, not every day.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Which is the best drink when you are thirsty?
questions.explanation: Clean water is the best drink. Fizzy drinks are treats and sweets are not a drink.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Tap the healthy snacks.
questions.explanation: Bananas, carrots and apples are healthy snacks. Sweets, chips and doughnuts are treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Match each food to its group.
questions.explanation: Rice gives us energy to go. Fish helps us grow strong. Carrots help us glow and stay healthy. A lollipop is only a treat.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Go, grow or glow? Sort the foods.
questions.explanation: Go foods give us energy: rice and potato. Grow foods help us grow strong: fish and eggs. Glow foods keep us healthy: carrots and bananas.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: We drink clean ___ every day.
questions.explanation: Our body needs clean water every day to stay healthy.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Healthy food gives us energy to play.
questions.explanation: Yes. Food gives us energy to run and play, and it helps us grow.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Sweets are good to eat every day.
questions.explanation: No. Sweets, chips and fizzy drinks are treats. Eat just a little, and not every day.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Put Shopon's story in order.
sequence: Shopon eats chips and a fizzy drink.
Mother packs roti, egg, banana and water.
Shopon has lots of energy to play.
questions.explanation: Chips and a fizzy drink left Shopon tired and hungry. A tiffin with roti, egg, banana and water gave him lots of energy.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Mother packs Shopon's tiffin. Which is best?
questions.explanation: A banana is a healthy fruit. Chips and doughnuts are treats, so they are not good for every day.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: It is Imran's birthday. How much cake is a good treat?
questions.explanation: Cake is a treat. A small piece is fine on a special day, but too much sugar is not good for our teeth or body.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Priya has rice for lunch. Which grow food can she add?
questions.explanation: Fish helps us grow strong. Rice is a go food, so adding fish makes a better meal. Sweets and lollipops are treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Tap the foods for a healthy lunch.
questions.explanation: Rice, fish and vegetables make a healthy lunch with go, grow and glow foods. Sweets and fizzy drinks are only treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Grow foods help us ___ strong.
questions.explanation: Fish, eggs, milk and dal are grow foods. They help our body grow strong.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Favourite fruit: mango 6, banana 4, apple 2. Which is most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 6 is more than 4 and more than 2. Mango is the favourite.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Which one is only a treat?
questions.explanation: A lollipop is a treat. We eat just a little, not every day. Apples and carrots are healthy.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: We should drink clean water every day.
questions.explanation: Yes. Water keeps our body healthy. It is the best drink.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Roti is Go. Egg is Grow. Which Glow food can we add?
questions.explanation: An apple is a glow food. Roti, an egg and an apple make a balanced meal. Doughnuts and cookies are treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Which lunch has go, grow and glow foods?
questions.explanation: Rice is go, fish is grow and carrot is glow, so that lunch has all three. The first lunch has only go foods and the last has only treats.

questions.title: Healthy Food
questions.stem: Tap the foods that give us energy to go.
questions.explanation: Rice, roti and potato are go foods. They give us energy to play. Eggs help us grow and carrots help us glow.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Sort the pictures. Day or night?
questions.explanation: We see the sunrise, the Sun and go to school in the day. At night we see stars and the Moon, and we sleep in bed.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Which one do we see in the sky at night?
questions.explanation: We see the Moon and the stars in the night sky. The Sun shines in the day.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Match the weather to what we need.
questions.explanation: We use an umbrella in the rain, cool water when it is sunny and hot, a warm scarf when it is cold, and a kite when it is windy.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Rain is falling. What should Mina take to school?
questions.explanation: An umbrella keeps the rain off. Ice cream and a ball do not help in the rain.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: At night, we can see the Moon and the ___.
questions.explanation: At night the sky is dark and we may see the Moon and the stars.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Put the times of the day in order.
questions.explanation: The day starts with the morning, then comes the bright day, and then it is night.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: In the day, the ___ lights up our sky.
questions.explanation: The Sun gives us light in the day. At night it is dark.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The Sun shines at night.
questions.explanation: No. The Sun shines in the day. At night the sky is dark and we may see the Moon and stars.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Tap the pictures that show weather.
questions.explanation: Sunny, rainy and windy are kinds of weather. A bed and a school are not weather.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The Sun shines on this side. Is it day or night?
questions.image_alt: The Sun on the left shines on the Earth. The side facing the Sun is marked DAY and the dark side is marked NIGHT.
questions.explanation: It is day on the side of the Earth that faces the Sun. The other side is dark, so it is night there.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Which one is the full Moon?
questions.explanation: The full Moon is the big, round, bright Moon. A thin Moon looks like a smile, and a new Moon is dark.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: In 10 days: 5 sunny, 3 cloudy, 2 rainy. Which was most?
questions.explanation: Count and compare: 5 is more than 3 and more than 2. There were most sunny days.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: It is a cool winter morning. Tap what Priya can wear.
questions.explanation: In the cool season we wear warm clothes like a coat and a scarf. An umbrella is for rain and a ball is for play.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Mitu wants to see the thin new Moon. When should she look?
questions.explanation: We can see the Moon at night, when the sky is dark. Mitu's family looks for the thin new Moon to know when Eid begins.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Windy days are good for flying kites.
questions.explanation: Yes. The wind lifts a kite up high. A calm day makes it hard to fly a kite.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Match each season to what it is like.
questions.explanation: In Bangladesh, summer is hot, the rainy season has lots of rain and winter is cool.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The seasons come back every year.
questions.explanation: Yes. Summer, the rainy season and winter come again and again. This is a pattern we can count on.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: Example: sunny, cloudy, rainy, sunny, cloudy. What comes next?
questions.explanation: Look for the pattern: sunny, cloudy, rainy, then it starts again. After cloudy comes rainy.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: It is noon, but dark clouds fill the sky. Is it night?
questions.explanation: Clouds can make the day look dark, but the Sun is still in the sky at noon, so it is day.

questions.title: Day, Night and Seasons
questions.stem: The Moon looks a little different from night to night.
questions.explanation: Yes. Some nights the Moon is a thin smile and some nights it is round and bright.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Sort the places. Natural or built by people?
questions.explanation: Forests, rivers and hills are natural places. Houses, schools and cities are built by people.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which place is natural?
questions.explanation: A hill is a natural place. Nature made it. A school and a hospital are built by people.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which place is built by people?
questions.explanation: People build houses to live in. A river and a hill are natural places.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Tap the things we get from nature.
questions.explanation: We get water, wood and fish from nature. A car and a TV are made by people in factories.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Match each old thing to its new use.
questions.explanation: We can reuse old things. A tin can makes a pencil pot, a bottle makes a plant pot and a box makes a toy car.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: We put rubbish in the ___.
questions.explanation: Rubbish goes in the bin. It must not go on the ground or in the river.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Reduce, reuse and ___ to help our Earth.
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less, reuse means use again, and recycle means make old things into new things.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: A river is a natural place.
questions.explanation: Yes. Nature made rivers. People did not build them.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Rubbish in the river is good for fish.
questions.explanation: No. Rubbish makes the water dirty and fish cannot live there. Keep our river clean.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Put the river clean-up story in order.
sequence: Children see rubbish in the river.
They pick it up and put it in bags.
They put up a "Keep our river clean" sign.
questions.explanation: The children saw rubbish in the river, picked it up with their teachers, and then the river was clean. Then they put up a sign.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Mina has an empty bottle. Where does it go?
questions.explanation: Rubbish goes in the bin. In the river it would hurt the fish and make the water dirty.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Nadia goes shopping. What can she take to carry things?
questions.explanation: A cloth bag can be used again and again, so we use less plastic.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Joy wants to help nature. What is a good idea?
questions.explanation: Planting a tree is kind to nature. Trees give shade, food and homes for birds. Rubbish and wasted water hurt nature.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Sort the actions. Kind to nature or hurts nature?
questions.explanation: Binning rubbish, taking a cloth bag and planting a tree are kind. Spilling oil, dirty smoke and bottles on the ground hurt nature.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which one makes the air dirty?
questions.explanation: Smoke from a factory makes the air dirty. A growing tree makes the air cleaner, and a cloth bag makes no smoke.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Match each word to what it means.
questions.explanation: Reduce means use less. Reuse means use it again. Recycle means make old things into new things.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: This place was built by people.
questions.explanation: Yes. A hospital is a building that people built to help sick people get better.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Which is the best thing to do with an old bottle?
options: Use it as a plant pot
questions.explanation: We can reuse a bottle as a plant pot. Throwing it in the river or on the road makes a mess and hurts nature.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: Children throw rubbish in a river. What can happen to fish?
questions.explanation: Rubbish makes the water dirty, so fish can get sick and cannot live there. Our choices can hurt living things.

questions.title: Our Environment
questions.stem: We get fish and wood from nature.
questions.explanation: Yes. Fish live in rivers and the sea, and wood comes from trees. We use many things from nature.
